notes.text: The forecast does not go short in the nine week window. Low point is $57,048 the week of 10/23. Opening cash is $87,522, down from $148,696 last week, so the forecast runs from a materially lower base. Committed watchlist spend inside the window is $16,400. The PEP floor plan payoff of $29,903 comes due 11/29, roughly five weeks past the end of this window.

Two sales carry signed purchase agreements, FS2:056 and WW:6D, and neither has a closing date so neither is in these numbers. Identified pipeline totals $111,500. Weekly timing comes from eight weeks of actual cash flow; levels come from the Fiscal Year Budget.

cfo_summary: Total available cash is $42,522 against a true bank balance of $87,522, the lowest available position in sixteen weeks. After $5,512 in external payments, projected end of week is $37,010. Ten bills, no intercompany transfers.

Available cash fell $48,161 in one week on a $5,288 bill run. Countryside accounts for $68,615 of the movement, a one time loan to GRP that does not recur. Group Group took in $45,000 of park distributions on 8/21 and paid out Tim's distribution before 8/28, returning to $87. Both are explained and neither changes the forward run rate.

GRP recovered fully. Available moved from negative $51,072 to positive $6,397 with no uncleared transactions, the cleanest GRP position since June. The Countryside loan funded that recovery, so the underlying pattern of GRP paying closing costs on behalf of the property entities is unchanged and will recur.

Six of nine entities are below $6,600. Country Aire projects to $1,446, Decade Acres to $3,036, Riverside to $4,514, RMF to $4,620, Winterwood to $6,237 and Countryside to $5,120. Group Group sits at $87. No entity has meaningful capacity to fund another entity this week, which is a change from every prior week where Countryside was the backstop.

The forecast does not go short in the nine week window, bottoming at $57,048 on 10/23. Committed watchlist spend inside the window is $16,400: the WW:11A roof at $5,900, the FS1:23 demo at $3,500 and the WW:6D lien release at $7,000.

Rico has been on the watchlist five weeks at $7,110 for the 44 Waterway rehab and did not appear on this run. The 8/10 review had it three quarters complete. Status needs confirming. WW:25A is new this week with $1,829 already paid through GRP and no scope on record.

Two homes carry signed purchase agreements. FS2:056 is in financing with the Vincent lien to be paid from buyer loan funding rather than GRP cash. WW:6D awaits appraisal and carries a $7,000 lien to Vincent on closing. Neither has a date. Home Tracker lien amounts remain blank, so no net proceeds figure can be produced on any sale.

The PEP floor plan note comes due November 29. Principal is $27,687.48 at 16 percent on the Swearingen buyback, now 2125 Patricia, with a payoff of roughly $29,900 including interest. The home is listed at $35,000, so a sale before the repayment date retires the note and nets GRP about $5,100. Two homes carry buyback exposure beyond that: WW:11A at $60,000, where a voluntary surrender was submitted and GRP is funding a $5,900 roof to prevent it, and Decade Acres 54 at $30,405 with the borrower 54 days behind.

for_ownership.label: Projected end-of-week cash
for_ownership.paragraph: We close this week at roughly $37,000 available across all accounts after a light bill run of $5,500. Available cash dropped sharply this week, but both causes are known: Countryside made a one time loan to Golden Rule Practices to clear its overdraft, and Group Group paid out your distribution. Golden Rule Practices is now fully recovered and clean for the first time since June. The portfolio is thin across the board this week, with six of the nine accounts under $6,600, so there is no obvious source if something unexpected comes up before rent lands next week. Looking out sixty days the business covers itself without needing a home to close, though two homes are under contract and would improve the picture.

floor_plan.note: Swearingen buyback. Promissory note dated 5/29/26, principal $27,687.48 at 16 percent, six month term, prepayable without penalty. Payoff shown includes accrued interest. Home listed 8/10 at $35,000; a sale before the repayment date retires the note and nets GRP roughly $5,100.

exposure.note: Older couple, current with GRP and with PEP. Tenant submitted a voluntary surrender form citing mold exposure; Justin inspected and found no mold. The surrender has not gone through. GRP is funding a $5,900 roof repair to prevent the buyback and the tenants are repaying GRP. The $60,000 is exposure avoided, not cash expected. Roof cost sits on the watchlist.
Payoff $30,405 as of end of July. PEP notified Justin the borrower was 54 days behind. Next due date read 7/01, suggesting a promise to pay, so she may return to the delinquency report. No date.
